extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners at the intersection of NLP, multimodal AI, and patent analysis (including patent offices)
extracted.subtask_description: A survey of methods, datasets, evaluation measures, challenges, and future directions for applying NLP and multimodal AI to patent tasks (classification, retrieval, quality analysis, generation). Useful for researchers building models and patent offices adopting AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification: multi-label hierarchical formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent classification is a multi-label classification where the classification scheme is hierarchical (IPC/CPC) and a single patent can be assigned multiple labels across levels (section, class, subclass, group, subgroup). The paper gives the formal formulation: patents (xi, yi) with yi a binary multi-label vector over classes C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must capture dependencies between broad and fine-grained categories and handle hierarchical structure. Inputs may come from different patent sections (title, abstract, description, claims); due to long full-text documents, models should identify the most relevant sections for classification. See Appendix A.3.1 for formal notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent classification evaluation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation measures for patent classification are accuracy, precision, recall, and the f1 score on the CPC or IPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting must indicate hierarchy level (section/class/subclass/group/subgroup) and dataset used (CLEF-IP, USPTO, WIPO, etc.) because dataset subsets, class hierarchies, and evaluation metrics differ and limit direct comparisons. Some works also report top-k metrics (e.g., top-3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design desiderata for classification models (use of PLMs and domain adaptation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent text differs from usual text; pre-trained language models (PLMs) fine-tuned on patent datasets (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa, SciBERT, XLNet, SBERT) often improve classification performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fine-tune PLMs on patent corpora (domain-adaptive pretraining, linguistically informed masking). SciBERT-based representations may outperform vanilla BERT for technical language. Report gains and baselines; note that large LLMs/PatLMs may be underexplored in classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent retrieval task formulation and ranking objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a query patent q and a set of patents X, compute a similarity score s(xq, xi) (e.g., cosine) and return a ranked set R(q) of top-k highest-similarity patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations may use sentence embeddings, PLMs, knowledge-graph embeddings (e.g., TransE) and combine text and image features for multimodal retrieval. Explicitly state similarity function, ranking cutoff (top-k), and retrieval pooling/merging strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent retrieval technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Key technical requirements reported include query expansion and identification of semantically similar documents, plus merging results from multiple search resources/databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems should support query expansion (alternate terms, synonyms), semantic matching across paraphrases, and robust result merging (e.g., via machine-learned rankers, RF, SVR). Document the query construction method and merging algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent retrieval evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Common retrieval metrics used in the literature include mean average precision (mAP), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multimodal retrieval also report modality-specific metrics and mAP; specify dataset (DeepPatent, DeepPatent2, EPO, USPTO) and whether evaluation is on text, image, or combined retrieval. Note that dataset differences limit cross-paper comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges and desiderata for patent image retrieval
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent images are typically black-and-white technical sketches with numeric labels and non-natural image characteristics, making retrieval and understanding harder than natural images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use models suited for technical drawings (vision transformers, CLIP, ResNet variants, specialized metric learning losses such as InfoNCE/ArcFace). Consider specialized preprocessing and evaluate using sketch/drawing benchmarks; report fusion strategy when combining with text (late fusion, contrastive alignment, dual encoders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality analysis indicators (features used to estimate value/quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonly used indicators for patent quality/value include forward and backward citations, number of claims, grant lag, patent family size, remaining lifetime (maintenance period), investor reaction, and various composite patent indices (e.g., OECD indices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the weight of each indicator is ambiguous, studies apply regression/classification models (linear, ridge, RF, XGBoost, MLP, CNN, LSTM). Explicitly list indicators used and justify selection; consider feature engineering from text, metadata, citations and metadata integration (knowledge graphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent quality evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality/value prediction studies report RMSE, MAE, MSE, Accuracy, Kappa, Precision, Recall, F1 and other task-appropriate metrics depending on regression or classification framing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly whether the task is regression (predict citation counts/value) or classification (quality buckets, maintenance categories). Acknowledge absence of a universal gold standard and report multiple complementary metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent generation task formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent generation is formulated as producing one part of a patent yi from input xi (e.g., generate abstract/first claim from title/description), modeled as yi = G(xi; θ) where G is the generation model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which patent parts are input vs. output (claim-to-specification, claim+drawing-to-specification, etc.), training data sources, and any multimodal inputs (drawings). Provide exact generation prompts/instruction formats used for LLMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desired qualities of generated patent text (factual, legal, novelty, clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated patent text should be factually accurate, legally correct/robust, novel (non-infringing), clear, and include desirable drafting features (e.g., appropriate claim length and limiting terms). The survey states PLMs/LLMs can hallucinate and produce repetitive or legally weak text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic n-gram metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) are insufficient. Use retrieval-based evaluation to check consistency with prior art, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for grounding, RLHF to align outputs with expert preferences, and involve patent attorneys/examiners for human evaluation on novelty, clarity, and legal robustness. When using RLHF, incorporate reward components for claim length and inclusion of limiting terms as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation approaches for generated patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested evaluation approaches include retrieval-based evaluation (consistency with prior art), retrieval-augmented generation (for grounding), and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) with patent experts to reduce hallucinations and improve legal robustness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design human evaluation protocols with criteria such as novelty, legal correctness, clarity, and reference-checking against existing patents; combine automatic grounding checks (retrieval similarity) with expert judgments. Report inter-annotator agreement and the specifics of any reward function used in RLHF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimodal learning desiderata for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are multimodal (text + images/drawings); aligning textual descriptions with technical images/drawings can provide richer representations for classification, retrieval, generation, and quality analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt multimodal encoders (CLIP-style, BLIP-2, joint text-image transformer architectures) and explicit fusion strategies (late fusion, contrastive alignment, dual encoders). Account for drawing-specific characteristics (geometric/line-art features) and evaluate multimodal performance against single-modality baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-jurisdictional retrieval considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-jurisdictional retrieval (e.g., USPTO vs EPO) presents challenges due to differences in legal terminology, language, classification codes, and document formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop cross-lingual/domain adaptation methods, map/classify across CPC/IPC code differences, and evaluate generalizability across jurisdictions. Explicitly report corpus provenance and pre-/post-processing steps for cross-jurisdictional tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent assessment and search-query construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing novelty often requires retrieving similar patents; generating effective search queries (alternate terms, related words, synonyms) is a key subtask that impacts retrieval relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mechanisms for synonym expansion, domain-specific thesauri, or automatic query reformulation. Report query generation strategy, seed terms, and any human-in-the-loop steps used to craft search queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset and benchmarking standards
rubrics_metrics.description: There are multiple publicly-used datasets with different formats and intended tasks (USPTO-2M, USPTO-3M, BIGPATENT, DeepPatent, DeepPatent2, HUPD, IMPACT, PatentMatch). Dataset differences (size, modality, preprocessing) affect evaluation and comparability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting results, explicitly name dataset(s), data splits, preprocessing steps, and tasks (classification, retrieval, summarization, generation). Prefer standardized benchmarks and provide code/data splits to enable reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of automatic evaluation and need for human-in-the-loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, citation-prediction proxies) are insufficient for assessing legal correctness, factual accuracy, or commercial value; LLM outputs require human oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design evaluation pipelines with domain experts (patent examiners/attorneys) for final validation, use retrieval-augmented checks against prior art to reduce hallucinations, and report limitations and ethical considerations (e.g., displacement risks).
